posts.author: FolkiFolki
posts.body:
It's been a while since my last thread, given that barely any issues had gotten in my way. I regret to inform you this time something did happen.
In my game, i have come up with the idea of multiple possible cutscenes depending on the player's choices. It had been working pretty well until now. I have one variable that changes between each specific cutscene. This is the one causing me trouble:
"Jess alts".
As you can see, once the cutscene is over, the variable changes to six. Now, because the variable is six, the new dialogue with the variable conditions to this specific variable set to six should play. I'm talking about this one:
But not only does this NOT show up once interacting with the npc, it plays out this one random dialogue that should only appear once the same variable is set to 2:
Once advancing through the story, THEN the intended dialogue with the variable 6, that is not supposed to show up anymore, decided to do so only then.
What in the tarnation? What?
I'm so utterly confused. I tried looking up what could possibly be messing up with the variables, inspecting the events carefully, but the earliest cutscene setting the variable to six should be working, but it simply doesn't.
Event though, some days ago, it was working perfectly fine, and i confidently remember not messing with any of the events. The time i didn't spend making the new cutscenes were spent making new maps, and it just doesn't make sense to me why this is happening.
I'm really hoping this is just a dumb little mistake i made. Any help would be immensely appreciated.

posts.author: bgillisp
posts.body:
What are the pages after page 4? It runs the highest valid page, so you may have duplicated page 2 later on with another condition.
Also its possible you got something else adjusting that variable in say a parallel process that is running after the cutscene, which would reset it back to something else. May need to use the search function in the engine to find uses of that variable to check.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
To add to that: The engine always reads only the page with the highest ID, that has their conditions met. So if there is a page with a higher ID than 4, with a condition that is  met before that if page 4 is met (like a lower value of the same variable), then page 4 will never run.
When you think something is wrong with your variables and you get an unexpected result, you can simple add a text message, saying "\v[2]" to show the value of this variable. This will help a lot in finding where the mistake lies. Just don't forget to delete that message after.
When on the map, you can also press F9 to open a menu that shows all values of variables and switches in your game. (At least, in MV it is F9, I assume it is the same key in MZ.)

posts.author: woootbm
posts.body: Something you might want to check is your plugins. Some plugins will use the game's variable database in their code. For example, you could have a lighting plugin that's reserved the same variable and is making changes to the lighting by increasing and decreasing that variable every X ticks.

posts.author: Andar
posts.body:
It can't be the page priority, because page 2 and page 4 have similar conditions and page 4 has higher priority. So the only way for page 2 to be active is if the value of the variable is lower than 6 but higher ot equal than 2.
so basically you need to find out what changed the variables value.
Use the editor search function for all uses of that variable - if it is used somewhere else in an event that is a parallel process, then this can happen.
if that search does not find additional events using the variable, then the variable was changed by script commands, either in the event command "script" or in a plugin.
The plugin option is more likely as there are a lot of plugins that use variables to exchange data and commands with the engine.
And that is why you always have to configure all plugins completely on adding them:
if a plugin uses such a procedure, it has a property line for the ID of a variable (or more than one) assigned to a plugin function.
On adding such a plugin you need to point that toward an unused variable and then name that variable as a sign that it is in use and where/for what.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Just deleting and remaking the event/variable might solve the issue for now... But it doesn't undo the mistake made. You actually should know why it showed the wrong page, and how that happened. If you don't find this out now, you might walk into larger problems later.
This could simply be a typo somewhere, in which case remaking it would solve everything, but if there is something working in the background, this problem isn't actually solved, but just out of sight. When the problem returns further down the development process, you might find out you have to redo pretty much everything.
Did you try pressing F9 to see what value was actually stored in the variable? This is really the first step to finding the problem.
Remember that debugging is never fun and can sometimes be very frustrating. But it is part of the job and can't be skipped or ignored, or you will end up with a buggy game.

Except that simply doesn't work that way. If you have multiple event pages with no conditions, it doesn't matter whether the contents will ever be executed or not based on a Conditional Branch - the earlier pages will
never
happen. The engine only looks at the highest-numbered page that meets its conditions.
Events don't just refuse to play, something is wrong in your project. Either it's the wrong event type, a variable isn't set up how you think it is, a condition is wrong, something.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
Okay, I am thinking outside the box here... is it possible le you made a back-up copy of your map?
Is it maybe possible your character is on the backup map, while you work on the main map, or the other way around? That would explain everything.
Or... If you load a saved game, some plugins might show the old version of the events when loading the game. To fix this, simply leave the map, and return. Or turn of that plugin.
then there is another possibility... some plugins change so much to the game, that saved test runs are no longer working at all. Or show unexpected results. If this error started after installing a plugin, the first thing you should try is delete /saves/ from your project folder. Then start a fresh new test run.

posts.author: JohnDoeGames
posts.body:
You don't make back ups? Well, that is not the question here, but I still advice you to do this as often as you can.
Plugins are not troublesome, if written correctly. However, plugins change how the engine works. So to achieve one goal, plugins might have to alter something else.
Plugins are also not written to work with each other available plugin.
In 99.9% of all cases, plugins are the solution, but sometimes they are the problem. That is very possible

on top of what JohnDoe said, it should be one of the first parts of troubleshooting a possible issue.
The engine functions a certain way that we all have access to and can observe if we own the engine. Plugins are made with the intention of modifying how the engine functions in order to do something specific.
if something that works in a fresh project doesnt in your main one and disabling your plugins fixes it, then the easiest conclusion to draw is you have a plugin changing how that thing works beyond what youve expected. From there you can take steps to isolate the plugin in question and choose what to do from there.
